title: The increasing-path conjecture for higher-order majorization
statement:
For integers $n$ and $k$, let $s_1,\dots,s_{k-1}$ be real numbers and define

$$
S_k=\left\{(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n\mathrel{\middle|}x_1\ge x_2\ge\cdots\ge x_n,\ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i^j=s_j\text{ for }j=1,\dots,k-1\right\}.
$$

Let $a,b\in S_k$ satisfy $a\succ_k b$. **Increasing-path conjecture.** There is a continuous function $p:[0,1]\to S_k$ such that $p(0)=b$, $p(1)=a$, and $p(t_1)\succ_k p(t_0)$ whenever $t_1\ge t_0$. The conjecture asks whether every higher-order majorization relation can be realized by a continuous path that is monotone for $\succ_k$; the surrounding discussion shows that the known constructions do not generalize to the relevant cases, while the claim itself is not resolved here.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.5249

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2011).
source_name: Zarathustra Brady, “Inequalities and higher order convexity”, arXiv:1108.5249 (2011).
